## Summary

The 68080 FPU is a fully pipelined 3-operand unit with 64-bit floats and access to FP0–FP7 and E0–E23 through the BANK prefix.

## Details

- The 6888x: 80 bit, 4 nibbles exponent + 16 nibbles fraction. Not pipelined.
- The 68080: 64 bit, 3 nibbles exponent + 13 nibbles fraction.
- It is a 3 operand unit. It has access to 4 times as many float registers, FP0..7 & E0..23. This is done by the BANK prefix.
- Example: fmul.w e4,fp3,e5 ( bank 1,0,%01.110 & fmul.w d4,fp3 )
- Convert e4.w to float, multiply with fp3 and put result in float register e5.
- The FPU is a fully pipelined unit that can accept an instruction every clock cycle. When a result is needed that is not ready yet, it waits until it is ready. (mostly 6 ticks or more) The user does not have to keep track of anything.
- (picture page 96 of the original ([instruction-timing.md](instruction-timing.md)))
- You can make it fast by executing other instructions that are not dependent on the result in the mean while.

### Hardware float instructions

```asm
fabs fadd fcmp fdiv fint(rz) fmove(m/cr) fmul fneg fnop fscc fsgldiv fsglmul fsub fsqrt ftst
```

### Slow microcode float instructions

```asm
facos fasin fatan fatanh fcos(h) fetox fgetexp fgetman flog10 flog2 flogn fmod frem fscale fsin fsincos fsinh ftan ftanh ftentox ftwotox
```

- Register e23 gets overwritten during execution by these instructions.
- (fp0..fp3 are used in micro-code, but restored after)
- Note:
- &lt;ea&gt; can be Double format from/to data-register. Single was always possible.
- The 080 has no implementation of packed bcd real size. (same on 040 & 060)
- B-address registers can not be used. (yet?)
- Newer V4 cores uses all 64 bits with calculation & fmove.x
- Older V4 cores use 11 nibbles fraction.
- V2 core 2.17 use 8 nibbles fraction (more does not fit in the fpga)
- V2: The extended format has a different layout, see page 83 of the original ([fpu/fmovem.md](fpu/fmovem.md)) fmovem.
- So the accuracy of the V2 is 1 / 4.000 million.

## Differences from AmigaOS / AROS / 68060

- The 6888x uses 80-bit floats and is not pipelined. The 68080 uses 64-bit floats and is fully pipelined.
- Packed BCD real is not implemented (as on the 68040 and 68060).
- The microcoded transcendental instructions overwrite E23.

## Do / Don't

- DON'T keep data in E23 across a slow microcode float instruction (facos, fsin, fetox, ...): it gets overwritten.
- DO schedule independent instructions while waiting for an FPU result (mostly 6 cycles or more).
- DON'T use B address registers in FPU `<ea>`.
